executiveSummary: The AI Hub website is live, Summer AI Institute programming was delivered successfully, and the August 5 University Advancement hands-on AI build workshop was delivered. Julian reported that the Advancement workshop was successful; participant outcomes and a continuing service commitment are not established. The Advisory Board memo awaits final senior approval, while research-support concepts and the DS&AI student consulting model remain bounded planning and pilot work.
priorities: Await final senior approval of the AI Hub Advisory Board memo; membership and invitations remain unapproved
Develop one initial faculty-centered AI for Research Lunch and Learn for peer sharing and needs discovery
Keep catalytic research support and a faculty research AI champion exploratory until need, authority, resources, scope, safeguards, and appropriate outcomes are defined
Confirm access, funding, project ownership, validation, and continuity controls before experimental DS&AI student consulting pilot work begins
Preserve public review, approval, delivery, commitment, and evidence boundaries

risks.statement: Draft materials could be mistaken for approved policy or broad service availability.
risks.mitigation: Keep draft and review labels visible and publish only through an authorized route.

risks.statement: AI advisory work could be misunderstood as replacing established shared governance.
risks.mitigation: State advisory limits explicitly and recognize existing authorities.

risks.statement: A future workshop could face access, network, pacing, or login issues if participant-path testing and a fallback are not completed.
risks.mitigation: Apply the Summer AI Institute lesson: test the complete participant path and maintain a safe no-login fallback before delivery.

risks.statement: New commitments could exceed available capacity if they are added without identifying what they displace.
risks.mitigation: Avoid adding commitments without identifying what they displace and protect scheduled delivery work.

risks.statement: The shared consultation model could be described inaccurately as GAABS-owned or GAABS-only.
risks.mitigation: Use shared-space language that recognizes Library facilitation and the broader consultation role.

risks.statement: The completed EDU-license rollout could be misrepresented as an effectiveness study even though it was not systematic or study-coordinated.
risks.mitigation: Describe available evidence only as descriptive adoption monitoring and require advance coordination before any future prospective evaluation.

risks.statement: Cross-system AI-readiness coordination could be interpreted as a UNCW commitment before scope or authority is clear.
risks.mitigation: Treat the July 22 discussion as exploratory coordination until participants, decision rights, expected contributions, and follow-up are documented.

risks.statement: Post-launch website content could be mistaken for approved policy or broad service availability.
risks.mitigation: Preserve review and ownership boundaries for future content and correct material issues promptly.

risks.statement: A possible educational agent could duplicate static guidance or imply endorsement before its purpose and maintenance model are clear.
risks.mitigation: Establish the article baseline, audience, source ownership, and agent-specific value before committing to build it.

risks.statement: The experimental DS&AI student consulting pilot could begin without confirmed access, funding, project ownership, validation, or continuity controls.
risks.mitigation: Confirm all five controls before pilot work begins; do not describe the model as a production service.

risks.statement: Student turnover could leave an early prototype without a maintainer.
risks.mitigation: Use peer learning, document handoff responsibilities, and name continuity ownership before implementation.

risks.statement: The first pilot could become too technically ambitious for its client need or cohort readiness.
risks.mitigation: Favor maintainable solutions and confirm project ownership, scope, and validation criteria before implementation.

risks.statement: Workshop delivery or reported success could be interpreted as participant-outcome evidence, effectiveness, or a continuing service commitment.
risks.mitigation: Report delivery separately from participant outcomes, effectiveness, and any future service commitment.

risks.statement: Catalytic research support or a faculty research AI champion could be interpreted as funded or approved before authority and outcomes are defined.
risks.mitigation: Keep both concepts exploratory until need, authority, resources, scope, safeguards, and appropriate outcomes are established.
